name: [R18] Request to PHPUnit's eval-stdin.php (CVE-2017-9841, CISA KEV)
message:
A request hit PHPUnit's Util/PHP/eval-stdin.php helper -- the entry point for CVE-2017-9841 (CVSS 9.8, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog). The bug is in PHPUnit itself, not application code, and becomes pre-auth RCE when a project's /vendor/ directory is mistakenly web-reachable. A public exploit (Exploit-DB 50702) probes many common vendor-directory prefixes with GET, then POSTs PHP code to the same path to run it.

This is one of the most common pieces of internet background-noise scanning for PHP-looking targets -- a single GET hit is not proof of exploitation or even that this host is vulnerable (only relevant if /vendor/ is actually served publicly here). Not related to PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619) despite both being PHP-related -- different bug entirely.

Confirm: is /vendor/ web-reachable on this host at all? If so, block it at the webserver/reverse-proxy level regardless of PHPUnit version, and check for a POST to the same path with an unexpected 2xx response as a stronger signal of actual exploitation.
